summary: The agent implemented most of the requested Map/iterable entry-mapping architecture and preserved all baseline behavior, but the hidden feature suite failed because generated code used wildcard-captured Map.Entry key/value types for lower-bounded map results. The agent's own lower-bound test only covered a mapping method declared to return AbstractMap.SimpleEntry, so it missed the requested case where a selected method has the concretely parameterized return type Map.Entry<String, String>.
quick_failure_summary: Generated iterable-to-map code does not compile for lower-bounded map results when the selected mapping method returns Map.Entry with concrete type arguments.

details.reasoning: JUnit reports 3641/3641 baseline tests passing and only 2/32 new tests passing. The 30 failures are compilation failures in generated EntryBoundaryMapper517e60Impl: the agent derives the local entry type from Map<? super String, ? super String>, producing Map.Entry<? super String, ? super String>. Calls to getKey()/getValue() therefore yield captured supertype values that cannot safely be passed back to put(). A correct implementation resolves the lower bounds to Map.Entry<String, String> (or otherwise uses the selected assignment's concretely parameterized entry type). The agent instead replaces the wildcard-derived type only when the selected return Type is non-abstract; Map.Entry<String, String> is an interface, so the replacement is skipped.
details.secondary_factors: The hidden class-level @WithClasses includes the failing boundary mapper for every main feature test, so this single compilation defect masks whether the other 14 feature behaviors would pass independently. That broad masking does not make the verifier broken because the mapper is valid, directly targets an explicit requirement, and fails deterministically. The agent's focused lower-bound regression test declared AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<String, Integer> as the mapping-method return type, which was narrower than the prompt's Map.Entry-oriented contract.

justification.issue_description: Lower-bounded map targets are converted into Map.Entry types using the wildcard TypeMirrors themselves, and the selected Map.Entry<String, String> return type is rejected as a usable concrete parameterization merely because Map.Entry is abstract/interface-typed.
justification.evidence: The prompt explicitly states: 'Compatible lower-bounded map result types are supported when the selected entry mapping method returns a concrete entry type.' It also consistently describes entry mappings in terms of Map.Entry<K, V>. Existing processor code resolves iterable wildcard element types through getTypeBound(), a pattern the agent itself retained in IterableMappingMethod and MapEntryMappingMethod. In the agent patch, TypeFactory.getMapEntryType uses typeArguments.get(...).getTypeMirror() rather than getTypeBound().getTypeMirror(), and MapEntryMappingMethod only adopts a selected Map.Entry return type when !returnType.isAbstract(). The hidden mapper's selected method is declared as Map.Entry<String, String>, and the generated-source diagnostics show Object/capture conversion errors at the map put call.
justification.verdict_reasoning: FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT is appropriate because lower-bounded result compatibility is expressly part of the task, and resolving wildcard bounds is a foreseeable requirement in this generic type-model codebase. This is not merely an undocumented hidden-test convention: the prompt calls out the case directly. It is also not a syntax or integration failure in the processor itself; the processor builds and baseline tests pass, but its generated-code logic is incomplete for the specified generic boundary.

problem_assessment.notes: This is a substantial compiler/model-generation task spanning method classification, generic type resolution, templates, forged mappings, qualifiers, and abstract Map.Entry construction. The lower-bounded requirement is terse, and 'concrete entry type' could have been clarified as a concretely parameterized static return type such as Map.Entry<String, String>, but the requirement itself is explicit and reasonably inferable from MapStruct's existing getTypeBound patterns. The tests are deterministic and the reference solution demonstrates solvability.

evidence: The baseline verifier completed successfully with 3641/3641 tests passing.

The new verifier reached processor-generated source compilation and reported deterministic capture-conversion errors in EntryBoundaryMapper517e60Impl rather than setup, import, dependency, service, or runtime failures.

The trajectory shows the agent successfully ran processor compilation, focused tests, adjacent suites, and Maven verify; there was no unresolved toolchain failure preventing implementation or validation.
The only minor tool friction was that rg was unavailable; the agent immediately switched to find/grep and continued, so this did not materially divert or block the solution.

The agent's own lower-bound test passed because its selected method was declared to return AbstractMap.SimpleEntry, confirming that the hidden failure is caused by a coverage and type-resolution gap in the implementation rather than an external execution problem.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker was found; the verifier exposes a deterministic generic type-bound defect in generated code.
